status: Hemp and hemp extract for human consumption are regulated by FDACS under Rule 5K-4.034, Florida Administrative Code. Cultivation is licensed by the FDACS Division of Plant Industry. This file records what state documents say; it never asserts the legal status of THC-A or any specific cannabinoid.

facts.label: Active hemp cultivation licenses on the state's published report
facts.source: FDACS Division of Plant Industry, Active License Report - HEMP (the report linked from the Hemp Cultivation Licensing page; the file's own title block is dated 4/24/2025)
facts.verify: 8-page PDF, hex-CID fonts; decode with the embedded ToUnicode CMap (equivalently glyph id + 29) and reconstruct rows from Td/Tm coordinates. 435 text rows, 431 unique license numbers (format YY_NNNNNN). This is the only active-license report FDACS publishes; the download id 92628 serves it regardless of the filename, so the 4/24/2025 date in the filename is the file's own currency.

facts.label: Florida counties with at least one licensed hemp cultivator
facts.source: Same FDACS Active License Report - HEMP
facts.verify: 357 of the 435 rows carry a county string matching Florida's official county list; the other 78 wrap across PDF lines and lose the field. 57 distinct counties appear among the parsed rows, so 57 is a floor, never a total: unparsed rows can only add counties. Leaders among parsed rows: Lake 31, Suwannee 21, Alachua 17, Hillsborough 16, Orange 15. Always state these as 'among rows that parsed', or use the floor framing.

facts.label: Hemp packages removed in five weeks of Operation Safe Summer
facts.source: FDACS press release, 'Commissioner Wilton Simpson Provides Update on Operation Safe Summer: Over 155,000 Illegal Hemp Packages Removed to Date', 28 July 2025
facts.verify: Release lists weekly totals: week 1 38,861, week 2 40,796, week 3 6,024, week 4 48,195, week 5 22,056, 'Total to date: Over 155,932'. The removals are for violations of Florida's child-protection standards for packaging, labeling and marketing. Report as packages removed for packaging and labeling violations, never as a product-safety or health finding.

facts.label: Hemp packages removed for violations since 1 July 2023
facts.verify: 'Since July 1, 2023, the department has removed over 800,000 packages of hemp products in violation of child-protection' standards. Use 'over 800,000' exactly; the release gives no precise figure.

facts.label: Enforcement date for the amended hemp rule
facts.source: FDACS press release, 'Commissioner Wilton Simpson Issues Reminder to Hemp Food Establishments on Upcoming Enforcement of Amended Rule', 2 June 2025
facts.verify: Rule 5K-4.034, Florida Administrative Code, governing hemp and hemp extract intended for human consumption. Amendments took effect 12 March 2025; FDACS announced 13 March 2025 that enforcement of the new provisions begins 16 June 2025. Named requirements include child-resistant packaging per ASTM D 3475-20, a prohibition on specified color additives, common household measurements for serving sizes, and a scannable barcode or QR code linking to the certificate of analysis, with the COA stating laboratory information and total delta-9 THC concentration.

facts.label: Counties inspected in the first week of Operation Safe Summer
facts.source: FDACS press release, 'Nearly 11,000 Hemp Products Removed ... in First Week of Operation', 24 June 2025
facts.verify: 'inspections of hemp retailers and manufacturers in 20 Florida counties and removed nearly 11,000 packages'. The 11,000 is week 1; the same operation's week-1 figure appears as 38,861 in the 28 July release, which counts packages rather than products. Do not add the two: they are different units in different releases. Prefer the July release's package series.

facts.label: Hemp products placed under Stop Sale Orders from one 2023 inspection
facts.source: FDACS press release, 'Historic Enforcement Actions Against Hemp Companies for Violations of Florida Law', 11 July 2024
facts.verify: Stop Sale Orders issued for 215,154 hemp products following an inspection on 31 October 2023. The release also describes a January 2024 reinspection finding relocated product. Name the enforcement action and its date; do not characterise any company beyond what the release states.

gaps: Count of licensed hemp FOOD establishments (the retail-facing permit under Rule 5K-4.034): FDACS publishes no list. The Hemp-Food-Establishment-Permit page 404s and the hemp program landing page is a soft 404 that returns HTTP 200 with 'page cannot be found' body text. Do not state a Florida hemp retailer count; the Texas figure has no Florida equivalent.
Florida hemp retail sales or market size: not published by any state agency found. Do not cite one.

Legal status of THC-A or any specific cannabinoid in Florida: not asserted anywhere on the page. FDACS documents describe packaging, labeling and COA requirements; they are not a statement of what may be sold. Any legality question goes to counsel.
City-level Florida hemp data: none published. County is the finest geography in the cultivation report, and 78 of 435 rows lose even that to PDF line wrap.

Newer enforcement totals: no 2026 hemp press release appears in the FDACS sitemaps as of 2026-08-25, so the 28 July 2025 update is the latest published total. Re-check before any claim about 'current' enforcement volume.
